rationale: While Sleyp et al. (2022) confirm that de novo missense variants in KLHL20 cause a syndromic neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by intellectual disability, febrile seizures or epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder (ASD), hyperactivity, and subtle facial dysmorphisms, the literature contradicts the claim that this constellation reliably differentiates KLHL20 from classic developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs) by phenotype alone. First, Sleyp et al. explicitly note that DEE itself was present in patients with KLHL20 variants (2 of 3 patients with non-recurrent missense variants), highlighting substantial phenotypic overlap with classic DEE entities. Second, the facial dysmorphisms in KLHL20 are described as 'subtle' rather than distinctively pathognomonic, making clinical prioritization from phenotype alone unreliable. Finally, no comparative cohort data against SCN1A- or STXBP1-related encephalopathies are provided in the literature to validate this hypothesized clinical filter.

evidence.text: Sleyp et al. delineated a neurodevelopmental syndrome in 14 individuals harboring de novo missense variants in KLHL20 (including 11 individuals with the recurrent c.1069G>A p.[Gly357Arg] variant), presenting with intellectual disability, febrile seizures or epilepsy, ASD, hyperactivity, and subtle dysmorphic facial features.

conflicts: Sleyp et al. (2022) found that 2 of 3 patients with non-recurrent missense variants in KLHL20 actually met criteria for developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE), demonstrating that KLHL20-related disease overlaps with and can present as a DEE.

Facial dysmorphic features in KLHL20 disorder are categorized as 'subtle', and no empirical clinical utility studies demonstrate that subtle dysmorphism combined with autistic/hyperactive traits can reliably distinguish KLHL20 cases from SCN1A- or STXBP1-related DEEs without exome/genome sequencing.

new_directions.question_text: Does 3D automated facial shape analysis quantitatively separate KLHL20-positive individuals from individuals with classic ion-channel or synaptic DEEs (such as SCN1A and STXBP1)?
new_directions.rationale: Because facial dysmorphism in KLHL20 is described as subtle, human clinical examination may not reliably distinguish it, but objective 3D dense-surface facial phenotyping algorithms could identify discriminating geometric features.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true frequency and distribution of detailed seizure types and EEG patterns in KLHL20 variants compared to SCN1A and STXBP1 cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether the epilepsy phenotype in KLHL20 is predominantly febrile/mild versus severe progressive DEE across a larger multicenter cohort will determine if neurophysiology provides a more specific discriminant than behavioral traits.
